thread: Jaina's deep reads cost her: numb hands and frost

evidence.clue: Frost-peeled knuckles from 'the last time she'd pushed too hard at a stone'.
At the culvert she loses her hand and her sense of the surface, takes three calls to come back; frost grows a hand's width round her palm and her skin peels.
The frost-sheet cast in the ambush takes the feeling from her right hand again.
Planned: 'a deeper read' at the Millhaven crossing, 'a good deal' deeper.

At the well the mage goes down with her left hand on the cobbles; frost runs into the cobble joints then forms a white plate round her hand; she does not respond to 'Mage', 'Proudmoore' or '*Proudmoore!*'; Sylvanas pulls the hand free and the skin tears ('A grey print of skin stayed on the frosted stone, four fingertips and the heel of a palm'); the skin of three fingertips is left raw and shining. She had asked to be called 'louder than last time... I went further than I meant to.'

At the storehouse frost spreads 'further than it had at the well'; she leaves skin on the boards again; the left fingers will only curl halfway ('stiff as a dead bird's foot'); the right hand is still dead.

Sylvanas bans hand-reads for the night ('You're done reading with those tonight'); Cyndia wraps both hands in linen strips; the mage reads thereafter by staff-heel only (in prints, horses, at the noon crossing).

Chapter 4: still no hand-reading (Sylvanas's ban holds, 'for once she had not argued'): she reads with the staff crystal held to bodies by Lyriel and her cheek to the ash. The cost shifts to wards: each holding ward draws a cold up the ash into her elbow, chest and the roots of her teeth; frost crust across the left knuckles by dusk; the left palm tears in the granary ('something in the hand gave') after the frost cast on Tam and the shell ward; arm 'ice from fingers to shoulder'; at night Lyriel cuts off black-red linen and finds a split in the heel of the hand 'an overripe plum'.

Chapter 4: left fingers curl only halfway; only two fingertips usable for the bandage knot; right hand still dead, staff carried in the crook of that arm. Slow return of feeling at dawn ('pins and then burning'). Jaina overrode Lyriel's 'leave it' to read the shell.

Chapter 6, morning: no reading by hand; the staff crystal runs 'the colour of straw left in the rain' (a clear gold in Dalaran), dipping with each pulse of the road's weight; guttering at the culvert. Little rest (slept sitting against a stone block), head aching since the fork; right arm dead and holding the staff against her ribs; left palm throbbing, the split pulling when she grips.

Chapter 6, afternoon: on the walled Andorhal approach the drag arrives 'behind her eyes as well as through the staff, and pushed' like diving deep at Boralus; ears hurting; teeth chattering in the heat; sweat; white frost on the bare fingertips creeping out over the linen; the crystal sinks until she can see the grain of the stone; a nosebleed (warm over the lip; the linen came away red); she refuses to dismount and keeps riding. First nosebleed on the page.

evidence_chapter7.clue: Chapter 7 (Sylvanas POV): at the gate Jaina's jaw is shut so hard a muscle jumps under her ear; dried blood in her nose; rust-stiff linen at the knuckles. In the shade of the arch her lip draws back as if the air had an edge.

Chapter 7: after reading every sample-room shelf she returns grey to the lips, hoarse and spending her voice carefully; the crystal at the head of the staff gives no light; two bare fingertips white to the first joint with frost furred on the linen on a warm night. She tried to write and got blots and a stroke through the paper; Corin wrote at her dictation.

Chapter 7: she offers a stated cost-limited ability: freeze one man's jaw before he can bite his collar, needing her fingers on his skin, once tonight ('I can only do it once tonight'). The risk is not yet tested.

notes_chapter7: Cost ladder continues: the sample-room day (many reads) costs more than a single deep read. Do not heal her hands. The jaw plan is the next payment. Heavy/clean reads work on sealed grain; a living man's skin is the next test.
notes_chapter6: Cost ladder: frost on bare fingertips and chattering teeth (Ch5) -> add nosebleed, pressure in the ears, crystal dimming to near-dark (Ch6). She cannot hear places she has not been; she feels Andorhal only because she is arriving. Do not heal the hands. Lyriel offers rest, Jaina refuses; next rung should be a real stop or a collapse.
readerKnows: Both hands are now damaged. The cost escalated rather than resetting. She reads by staff-heel and may be limited to that for some time.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas has seen the cost twice more and has limited it by order; she does not understand how it works.
notes_chapter4: Escalation continues: spell costs, not only deep reads, now hurt her (ward upkeep through the night, frost cast on a person, shell ward). The left palm is split in the heel at chapter end and rebound. Do not heal her hands before the next arc beat. The right hand is still dead.
notes: Hands wrapped in linen at chapter end; nausea and grey face after hard listening. Keep the escalation; do not heal her hands in the next chapter without cause.
